ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a large gray circle, with two white circles inside. The white circle on the left is larger, labeled with radius 3; the white circle on the right is smaller, labeled with radius 2. The two white circles are externally tangent to each other, and their centers are on the same horizontal line; the left white circle is tangent to the large circle at the far left, and the right white circle is tangent to the large circle at the far right. The gray shaded part is the region inside the large circle and outside the two white circles. Reasoning: The radii of the two inner circles are 3 and 2 respectively, and they are externally tangent, so the distance between the centers of the two circles is 3+2=5. Along the horizontal diameter direction, the diameter of the large circle is equal to the sum of the left circle radius 3, the distance between the centers of the two circles 5, and the right circle radius 2, namely 3+5+2=10, therefore the radius of the large circle is 5. Shaded area = area of the large circle − areas of the two inner circles = π·5^2−π·3^2−π·2^2=25π−9π−4π=12π.

raw_record.question_text: Circles of radius $2$ and $3$ are externally tangent and are circumscribed by a third circle, as shown in the figure. Find the area of the shaded region.

method.method_draft: Use the diagram to observe that the two white inner circles are tangent to each other and also tangent to the large circle at the far left and far right along the same horizontal line through their centers. From the text, their radii are 3 and 2, so the distance between their centers is 3+2=5. The full horizontal diameter of the large circle is the left radius 3, plus the center-to-center distance 5, plus the right radius 2, giving diameter 10 and large radius 5. Compute shaded area as area of the large circle minus the areas of the two inner circles: π·5^2−π·3^2−π·2^2=12π.

method.method_draft: Set up a collinear tangency equation from the figure. Let R be the radius of the large circle. The image shows the large circle internally tangent to the radius-3 circle on the left and to the radius-2 circle on the right, with the large circle’s center between the two small centers. Therefore the distance from the large center to the radius-3 center is R−3, and the distance from the large center to the radius-2 center is R−2. Since the two small circles are externally tangent, their center distance is 3+2=5, so (R−3)+(R−2)=5. Solve to get R=5. Then subtract the two small disk areas from the large disk area: πR^2−9π−4π=12π.
